chopin-op25-6-thirds.title: Étude in G-sharp minor, Op. 25 No. 6
chopin-op25-6-thirds.note: The right hand's trill in thirds, B–D♯ against C♯–E, breaks into a chromatic scale in thirds that climbs two octaves.

chopin-op25-8-sixths.title: Étude in D-flat major, Op. 25 No. 8
chopin-op25-8-sixths.note: Legato sixths in the right hand, rocking between F–D♭ and G♭–E♭ in triplet eighths, with the left hand in broken intervals below.

beethoven-op13-broken-octaves.title: Sonata No. 8 in C minor, Op. 13 “Pathétique”, I
beethoven-op13-broken-octaves.marking: Allegro di molto e con brio
beethoven-op13-broken-octaves.note: The start of the Allegro: the left hand drums broken octaves on C in eighth notes while the right hand enters with the theme.

liszt-mephisto-broken-octaves.title: Mephisto Waltz No. 1, S. 514
liszt-mephisto-broken-octaves.note: The right hand snaps each note to its upper octave in sixteenths, sliding down the keyboard over a repeated left-hand chord.

chopin-op25-10-octaves.title: Étude in B minor, Op. 25 No. 10
chopin-op25-10-octaves.note: Both hands in octaves, two octaves apart, creeping chromatically in triplet eighths from the very first beat.

chopin-op53-octaves.title: Polonaise in A-flat major, Op. 53
chopin-op53-octaves.note: The E-major trio's left-hand ostinato: octaves E–D♯–C♯–B in sixteenths, repeated under quiet right-hand chords.

liszt-mephisto-leaps.title: Mephisto Waltz No. 1, S. 514
liszt-mephisto-leaps.note: In the Presto the right hand plays a single note, then jumps to a double octave one or two octaves higher, over and over at full speed.

liszt-campanella-leaps.title: La campanella, Grandes études de Paganini S. 141 No. 3
liszt-campanella-leaps.note: The theme sits on the thumb while the little finger leaps up to the bell note D♯ between every melody note.

beethoven-op53-repeated-chords.title: Sonata No. 21 in C major, Op. 53 “Waldstein”, I
beethoven-op53-repeated-chords.note: The opening: pianissimo repeated eighth-note chords low in the keyboard, to be kept perfectly even and quiet.

chopin-ballade1-scale.title: Ballade No. 1 in G minor, Op. 23
chopin-ballade1-scale.note: Near the end of the coda both hands race up the G-minor scale two octaves apart in one sweep before the closing chords.

chopin-op10-1-arpeggio.title: Étude in C major, Op. 10 No. 1
chopin-op10-1-arpeggio.note: Sixteenth-note arpeggios on C major stretch a tenth in every group, climbing four octaves and coming straight back down over a left-hand octave.

liszt-hr2-broken-chords.title: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2, S. 244/2
liszt-hr2-broken-chords.note: In the Lassan the right hand pours broken C♯-major chords down and back up the keyboard in thirty-second notes.

ravel-alborada-repeated-notes.title: Alborada del gracioso, Miroirs No. 4
ravel-alborada-repeated-notes.note: The famous repeated-note passage: G♯ struck again and again in rapid triplet sixteenths, changing fingers on every note.

beethoven-op53-trill.title: Sonata No. 21 in C major, Op. 53 “Waldstein”, III
beethoven-op53-trill.note: The right hand keeps a trill going on G–A with its lower fingers while the upper fingers play the theme above it.
beethoven-op53-trill.manual_check: Melody matches a second edition; trill speed differs between editions

chopin-op10-11-tenths.title: Étude in E-flat major, Op. 10 No. 11
chopin-op10-11-tenths.note: Every chord is rolled and spans a tenth or more in each hand, with the melody on the top note of the right hand.

brahms-op118-2-three-two.title: Intermezzo in A major, Op. 118 No. 2
brahms-op118-2-three-two.note: The right-hand melody moves in plain eighths while the left hand rolls triplet arpeggios underneath: two against three on every beat.

chopin-op66-four-three.title: Fantaisie-Impromptu in C-sharp minor, Op. 66
chopin-op66-four-three.note: Right-hand sixteenths against left-hand triplet eighths: four notes against three on every beat.

chopin-op10-3-melody.title: Étude in E major, Op. 10 No. 3
chopin-op10-3-melody.note: The melody sits in the top fingers of the right hand while the same hand plays sixteenth-note accompaniment underneath it.
chopin-op10-3-melody.manual_check: Checked by hand against the Schlesinger first edition

chopin-op25-5-inner-voice.title: Étude in E minor, Op. 25 No. 5
chopin-op25-5-inner-voice.note: In the E-major middle section the melody moves into the left-hand thumb, in the middle of the texture, under right-hand arpeggios.

ravel-ondine-pedal.title: Ondine, Gaspard de la nuit No. 1
ravel-ondine-pedal.note: A pianissimo shimmer of repeated chords with the melody entering underneath: the pedal has to keep the haze alive without letting the tune blur.

schumann-toccata-endurance.title: Toccata in C major, Op. 7
schumann-toccata-endurance.note: Nonstop sixteenths in double notes that keep going for pages: the right hand alternates C–E with B–F without a single rest.
